decisions: Preserve worktree-swarm as the one-shot local compatibility utility.
Use land-by-wave as the safe default and integration-branch as explicit opt-in.
Require argv-only provider commands, ephemeral environment secrets, and ownership-token cleanup.
Use GitHub Actions ubuntu-latest runners as the recommended free VM provider; local VMs do not fit a 4 GB workstation.
Derive the worker body from the canonical TicketArtifact description, acceptanceCriteria, and validation fields, and keep tracker number and URL explicit.
Verify every landed issue commit is an ancestor of the new base before advancing a wave; squash merges are rejected.
Fence concurrent runs with expiring per-issue claims and make GitHub Actions dispatch find-or-dispatch idempotent.

validation.focusedTests: pass (23 fleet tests plus 10 DAG scheduler tests, including ticket normalization, claims, ancestry verification, local-worktree, vm-pool, integration-branch, and GitHub Actions provider units)

nextConsumer: parallel-issue-fleet validation and Core Flow routing
riskRemaining: GitHub Actions requires the workflow on the default branch, a repository secret for the model provider, and the gh workflow scope. No live workflow dispatch was executed in this environment. Claims are local to the state root, and land-by-wave requires merge or rebase commits rather than squash merges.
